_purpose: THE CONTRACT between the Dart and Python pricing engines. Every case lives here once; both suites load this file. A rule change means editing this file first, then making both sides pass. See CLAUDE.md hard rule 3.
_units: Dimensions are in tenths of a millimetre (tmm). Money is in sen. 1ft = 3048 tmm, 1in = 254 tmm.
_lock_grant_purpose: SPEC.md §6.1 and §13 B1. Client, Sep 2026: 'no second rm300 paid later in showroom, only depo at fair can lock price.' This is the only place a category_locks row is created, so the rule cannot be bypassed by a screen that forgets it. Both engines load these cases.

lock_grant_cases.why: The base case. RM300 at the fair buys twelve months of this category's prices.
'no second rm300 paid later in showroom, only depo at fair can lock price.' The money is still taken; it confirms the order and buys nothing else.
Same rule. Measuring at the customer's house is not a fair, however much it feels like a sale.
Four channels are not fairs, and each has to be refused by the same branch rather than by four screens remembering to.
The fourth. Listed on its own because a channel added later must not default into locking.
RM250 is not RM300. A partial payment must not buy a full twelve-month hold, and the amount is checked here rather than trusted from the screen that collected it.
A customer who hands over RM500 for one category gets the same hold. The extra is money on the order, not a longer or better lock.
'A rate lock pins BOTH held_rate_card_version AND held_discount_pct. Pinning only the version silently reprices held orders when the promo % moves.'
29 February has no anniversary. Clamped to the last day of the month, which is what every calendar does with a monthly anniversary and what a person reading '12 months' would say.
31 August exists next year too, so no clamping happens and the hold runs the full year.
The fencepost next to the clamp. 28 February exists every year, so it must not be dragged anywhere.
The other direction. A 29 February in the destination year is a real date and the hold should reach it.
'making it rm600 for both'. The second RM300 is a second row, not an extension of the first.
Three categories. Wallpaper needs its own RM300 and gets its own row.

_customer_key_purpose: SPEC.md §6.1 and §13 B9. Which customer a rate lock belongs to. The lock follows the customer, not the order -- a hold bought at last August's fair has to price a line added months later, on a new quote. It was keyed on the quote id, which meant the twelve-month hold could never match again and the customer was charged more than the hold they paid for. Both engines load these because a lock granted on a handset and a lock read back from the server have to agree about whose it is.
_customer_key_phone: Malaysian numbers arrive typed however the customer said them. Normalising is deliberately narrow: strip the punctuation people use, accept a +60 or 60 country prefix as a leading 0, and require at least nine digits. Anything less is treated as no phone at all, because a key built from a fragment would merge two customers, and merging two customers hands one of them the other's held prices.

customer_key_cases.why: The base case. The shop collects a phone; two quotes with the same phone are the same customer coming back.
One person types 012-345 6789 in August and 0123456789 in March. Treating those as two customers loses the hold they paid for.
The same, in the other shapes people write.
+60 12 345 6789 and 012 345 6789 are one number. A customer who gave the international form at the fair and the local one in the showroom must not lose their hold.
The same number with the plus dropped, which is how it arrives from a pasted contact.
060... is not a country code with a zero in front of it. Stripping one here would turn a real number into somebody else's.
A walk-in who gives no number. The lock still works within the quote it was bought on, which is no worse than the behaviour this replaces, and it never matches somebody else.
A field that was opened and left alone.

Somebody typed four digits and moved on. A key built from a fragment would collide with every other four-digit fragment and hand one customer another's held prices, so it is refused and the quote id is used instead.
The edge of the nine-digit floor, from below.
The same edge from above, so the floor cannot drift by one without a test noticing. An 03 landline is nine digits.
A name typed into the phone field. What is left after stripping is not a number, so it is not used as one.
The whole point. The August quote and the March quote produce the same key, so the hold bought at the fair prices the line added months later.

_price_override_purpose: SPEC.md §6.5. An admin moving a line's total by hand, and the audit row that is the actual control. The spec is blunt about why: 'An offline PIN is bypassable, and one shared admin password reaches every part-timer within a month. The real control is the audit log plus a weekly review screen, not the gate.' Both engines load these cases because the server re-validates an override before it accepts one -- an override the server refuses would otherwise leave a handset showing a price nothing else agrees with.

price_override_cases.why: The base case. RM552 down to RM500 with a stated reason, by somebody the log can name.
Nothing says an override is a discount. A line under-quoted by mistake is corrected the same way, and it gets the same audit row.
price_override_cases.reason: line was quoted at the wrong band

price_override_cases.why: A line written off entirely -- a remake, a goodwill fix. The spec sets no floor, so neither does this. It is the audit row that makes it survivable, and RM0.00 with a name and a reason against it is exactly what the weekly review is for.
price_override_cases.reason: remake at our cost, original was cut short

price_override_cases.why: A refund is a payment of kind refund (§6.4), not a line that costs less than nothing. Allowing it would make an order total that no invoice can explain.
Overrides are an admin power. Staff see rates and cannot edit them.
'Individual PINs so the log names a person.' An override with no user against it is not an audit trail, it is a number that changed. The admin flag alone is not enough.
'reason mandatory, minimum 4 characters. No empty-string bypass.'
The four-character minimum, at its edge.
The other side of the same edge, so the bar cannot drift by one without a test noticing.
Spaces pass a length check and say nothing. Trimmed before it is measured.
An audit row recording that RM552 became RM552 is noise, and noise is what stops the weekly review being read. The spec puts the whole control on that review being readable.
A closed or cancelled order has a number on a document the customer already has. Changing it now would make the paper and the database disagree, with nothing on either saying which came second.
A part-timer who is refused should be told they may not, not sent off to write a longer reason for something that will be refused anyway.

_order_status_purpose: SPEC.md §6.3. The pipeline an order walks after the deposit confirms it, and the guards on each step. Both engines load these cases, because the server re-validates every transition a handset pushes: a status that moved on one device and was refused on the server would leave the two disagreeing about whether a job is in production.
_order_status_lines: Each case carries the order's lines in the only four states the guards read: whether the line needs a site measurement, whether it has final dimensions yet, whether its material was deferred at quotation (SPEC.md §13 B7), and whether one has since been chosen.

order_status_cases.why: The first step of the normal path. Nothing to guard: booking a visit asserts nothing about the job.
The tape has been out and every line that needed it has final dimensions.
Five of six windows measured is not a measured order. Marking it so hands final pricing a line with no tape behind it, and quietly breaks the variance report the estimate exists for.
Every deferred material has been chosen, so the line can be priced at what the customer actually picked rather than at the dearest option in its group.
At final pricing a missing material raises rather than guessing; nobody is invoiced for a material they never picked. The status is the last place that is cheap to catch.
Cutting starts.
Made, and waiting on an installation slot.
Fitted in the customer's house.
Paid up and done. The last transition there is.
confirmed straight to in_production would mean cutting material for dimensions nobody took. Each skipped step is also a lie in the append-only history somebody reads a year later.

A supply-only order still passes through the visit steps, because nothing-needs-measuring is a judgement about the lines while the pipeline is a record of what happened. Refusing here is the conservative reading; whether supply-only orders skip ahead is SPEC.md §13 C7, to answer rather than guess.
A remeasure is new dimensions on the same order, not a rewind. Rewinding would let a second visit overwrite the first with no record that either happened.
The same rule one step further along, where the material has already been cut.
Two part-timers tapping the same button on one order, or one tapping twice on a slow handset. It writes nothing, and it is not a failure to show anybody.

Staying put is answered before terminal, so a second tap on a finished order is the same quiet no-op it is anywhere else in the pipeline rather than an error about the order being closed. The distinction only shows up here, which is why it is written down.
Reopening a closed order would put a second ending on a job that already ended.
A cancelled order that comes back is a new order. Un-cancelling one would leave the deposit attached to a history that says it was refunded.
The customer changes their mind the week after the fair. What happens to the RM300 is SPEC.md §13 B3 and unanswered; the status moves either way, and nothing here computes a forfeit or a refund.
Material is already cut, which is expensive and is exactly why it has to be recorded rather than blocked. The cost is a conversation, not a state machine.

Same rule as a price override, for the same reason: a cancelled order with a customer's deposit against it and no stated cause is the one B3 will have to adjudicate from. Four characters minimum, no empty-string bypass.
A three-letter shrug is the empty-string bypass wearing a hat.
Whitespace passes a length check and says nothing.
The curtains are on the customer's wall. Taking them down is a return, which this system does not model, and calling it a cancellation would put a fitted job in the cancelled column of every report.
The guards read the lines; cancellation does not. An order that somehow has none must still be closable rather than stuck in confirmed forever.

_rate_lock_purpose: SPEC.md §6.1: 'a line whose category has no active lock must not be priced at a held version. Silently applying a curtain lock to a flooring line is the expensive bug in this design. Write that test before the resolver.' These cases were written first, and both engines load them.
_rate_lock_pct: Discount percentages are exact rationals written as strings, the same as billed_qty. '1/10' is ten percent. Never a float: a percentage of a price is money, and money is never binary floating point.

rate_lock_cases.why: The base case. A fair customer paid RM300 for curtains and comes back inside the 12 months.
THE expensive bug. One RM300 was paid, for curtains. The flooring on the same order is not held and must not be priced as if it were.
Same unlocked flooring line, but in the showroom in March. No promo, no hold, the order's own pinned version.
'Blinds and tracks have their own rates but ride the curtain deposit.' family and deposit category are different fields.
Same mapping. A special track is charged on top of a curtain and belongs to the same RM300.
Three deposit categories, not two. Wallpaper needs its own RM300.
Self levelling is family 'service' and deposit_category 'flooring'. The rule's own answer wins over the family map, because a service belongs to the work it prepares.
A motor on a blind is charged on top of that blind. It cannot have a deposit category of its own, because it cannot exist on its own.
The same expensive bug, one level down. An add-on inherits its parent's category, including when that category is not the locked one.
Standing at the fair before any RM300 is paid. Fair prices apply today; nothing is held.
'Showroom pays standard.' No promo, no hold, and the version the order was created against so a mid-order publish cannot move the price.
Only the fair channel gets fair pricing without a deposit. A home visit is standard, like the showroom.
Twelve months and no more. An expired hold prices like no hold at all.
The fencepost. held_until is the last day the hold is good for, not the first day it is not: a customer who arrives on the final day was promised that price.
A cancelled hold is a row kept for the record, not a price.
The RM300 went back. The price it bought goes back with it.
'Pinning only the version silently reprices held orders when the promo % moves.' The promo has since gone from 10% to 20%; this customer keeps 10%.
No hold, so today's promo applies rather than anybody's held one.
'Promo and the 12-month lock are fair-only.' A promo running at a fair must not leak into a showroom walk-in.
Two RM300s were paid, at different fairs, so the two categories hold different versions. Each line takes its own.
The other half of the same order. Getting this wrong charges a customer last August's flooring prices, or this year's curtain prices.
The expensive bug wearing a different hat. A curtain hold that has run out must not quietly fall back to the flooring hold that has not.

cases.why: The base case. 12ft wide, 9ft high, under the 10ft band edge.
10ft 6in high crosses into the upper band. The RM144 step.
12ft 4in bills as 13ft on a quotation. A10.
THE fencepost. Exactly 10ft (30480 tmm) must price at RM46, not RM58. band_max_tmm is 30481, not 30480.
MVP substitutes RM40 for RM46. No percentage arithmetic anywhere.
A 3ft x 4ft roller is 12 sqft but bills the 18 sqft minimum.
10ft 1in is the upper band. Against golden-4, this is the RM144 swing the app exists to prevent.
One tenth of a millimetre past 10ft is already the upper band. Pins the constant itself, not just the price.
Whole-millimetre storage made 12ft into 3658mm, back into 12.0013ft, and up to 13ft — quoting RM598 against golden-1's RM552. Tenths removed the round-trip.
The same 12ft 4in window, measured on site, bills 12.3333ft not 13ft. Quote RM598.00, bill RM567.33.

cases.source: Open question A11a — ASSUMED, awaiting confirmation
cases.why: A site-measured 3ft x 4ft roller still bills the printed 18 sqft minimum, because a minimum quantity is a commercial floor and not a rounding artefact.
Three identical windows are 3 x round(qty x rate), not round(3 x qty x rate).
Zebra J/BL and TBL are different rates on the same variant. Material cannot be deferred past deposit for these.
A second banded variant, to prove the band logic is not hard-coded to night curtain.
MVP applies only to some products. A day curtain has no MVP rate, so an MVP customer pays standard — not an invented discount.

cases.source: Client instruction, Sep 2026 — material chosen at measurement
cases.why: At a fair the job is to lock the deposit, so nobody picks J/BL vs TBL. The two differ by RM3/sqft, and the quote promises the final can only fall, so the estimate must use the DEARER option (TBL RM15). Quoting J/BL would make the final go up, which is exactly what SPEC.md §8.5 says cannot happen.
Once the customer picks J/BL at measurement the line prices at RM12, RM90 below the deferred quote. That drop is the promise being kept, not an error.
Outdoor ZIP defers openness (1% RM55 vs 0% RM60) and carries a 30sqft minimum. The dearer option wins, and the minimum still applies on top.

cases.source: MITC price list — RM10/sqft, RM11/sqft over 10ft(H)
cases.why: Height bands are not a curtain-only idea. A per_sqft blind bands on height too, and here the height both selects the band AND multiplies, unlike per_ft_width.

cases.source: MITC price list — the row PDF text extraction orphaned
cases.why: Text extraction lost this row's label, leaving RM68/ft and RM75/ft unattached. Rendering the table at 300dpi showed it is MULTI TRACK, banded like the other tracks.

cases.source: MITC price list — Korea Wallpaper, buy 1 free 1, 14ft x 10ft, RM800 (2 roll)
cases.why: ANSWERED A14: RM800 buys two rolls covering 280sqft in total. A 20ft x 10ft wall is 200sqft, so one charge covers it. Pattern-repeat wastage is deliberately NOT applied — §13 A7 is unanswered and a guessed percentage would silently overcharge every wall.

A 30ft x 10ft wall is 300sqft, just over one 280sqft bundle, so it needs two. You cannot buy a fifth of a buy-one-free-one pair. This is the boundary that the 140-vs-280 reading moves, so it is pinned.

cases.source: Client, Sep 2026 — all SPC minimums are the same
cases.why: A13 answered. A 150sqft herringbone floor bills the 200sqft minimum like every other SPC row: 200 x RM8 = RM1,600, not 150 x RM8 = RM1,200.
An add-on priced per piece ignores dimensions entirely.

Self levelling is a service, and services default to the curtain deposit. This one must not: it is flooring work and belongs to the flooring RM300. Applying a curtain lock to it is the expensive bug in this design.

quote_total_cases.why: A single small roller blind quotes RM162, below the RM300 deposit. The quote shows RM300 with the uplift on its own row, never folded into the line.
Above RM300 the floor is inert.

quote_total_cases.source: Open question B8 — ASSUMED, diverges from per-order in Phase 2
quote_total_cases.why: Curtain RM250 plus flooring RM200 quotes RM600 under per-category, RM450 under per-order. Phase 1 carries one category only, so the readings agree here.
A RM162 blind floors to the RM300 deposit, and a RM100 transport charge is added on top of that, giving RM400. Travel is not a product, so the per-category floor must not drag it up to RM600.

quote_total_cases.source: MITC price list — KL, Seremban, Negeri Sembilan
quote_total_cases.why: The larger of the two zones, on a normal quote.
Only the two printed outstation zones charge. Everything else is local and free.
Final pricing is what it is. A quote of RM300 that measures down to RM240 lands in open question B4, not in a silent floor.
